newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish olive oil exports hit by price, duties.
newsitem.headline: Turkish olive oil exports hit by price, duties.

text.p: Turkey's olive oil producers said on Monday lower international prices and the government's slowness to scrap export duties were hampering efforts to export production from their record output in 1996/97.

"With pressure from foreign cartel groups, buyers reduced the price of olive oil to about $2,000 per tonne this year," said Cahit Cetin, head of olive oil department at Taris, the largest farm cooperative in Turkey.
"But the prices were between $4,000 to $4,200 last year," he told Reuters.
Cetin said Turkey would have a record olive oil output this year with 223,500 tonnes and could export about 180,000 to 200,000 tonnes.
"Permission should be given for the surplus to be exported otherwise farmers would not be able to take the burden next year," he said.

Turkey, which consumes about 40,000 tonnes of olive oil every year, has imposed an export duty of $175 per tonne since 1994. A draft decree prepared by the foreign trade undersecretariat to scrap the duty has been before the government since December.
Turkey exported olive oil worth about $100 million in 1996, some 30 percent lower than the previous year.
